record.context_brief: Simpler proof for small-ε Ginzburg-Landau uniqueness
record.original_question: Find a simpler proof of the theorem of Pacard and Rivière asserting that, for sufficiently small ε > 0, the radial solution Uε is the unique solution of the disk Ginzburg-Landau system -Δu = ε^{-2}u(1 - |u|^2), u=x on ∂Ω.

evidence.quote: When ε is sufficiently small: ε < ε0 for some appropriate ε0. This result is due to Pacard-Rivi`ere [PR]. Their proof is highly non-trivial and fills a significant part of the monograph [PR]; it would be interesting to find a simpler proof.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and for each $\varepsilon > 0$ consider the Ginzburg–Landau boundary value problem for maps $u : \overline{\Omega} \to \mathbb{R}^2$,
$$-\Delta u = \varepsilon^{-2}\, u\,(1 - |u|^2) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u(x) = x \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega.$$
It is known that this problem admits a radial solution $U_\varepsilon(x) = f_\varepsilon(|x|)\,\frac{x}{|x|}$, where $f_\varepsilon : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ satisfies $f_\varepsilon(0) = 0$, $f_\varepsilon(1) = 1$, and the corresponding ODE obtained by substitution. It is also known (a theorem of Pacard and Rivière) that there exists $\varepsilon_0 > 0$ such that for every $0 < \varepsilon < \varepsilon_0$, the radial solution $U_\varepsilon$ is the unique solution of this boundary value problem.

Problem: Provide a proof of this uniqueness statement that is substantially simpler than the original argument of Pacard and Rivière (whose proof relies on a long and technical analysis using weighted Hölder spaces and a delicate linearization study).
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has produced simpler and more direct uniqueness proofs in related settings: e.g., Ignat–Nguyen–Slastikov–Zarnescu established uniqueness of vortexless minimizers and of the degree-one vortex using Hardy-decomposition / positivity-of-radial-profile arguments. These results recover and simplify aspects of the Pacard–Rivière theorem, indicating substantial progress, though it is not clear that the full original statement has been reproven by elementary means.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of degree-one Ginzburg-Landau vortex in the unit disk
status_evidence.snippet: Uses positivity of radial profile and a Hardy-type decomposition to give a simpler uniqueness proof for the degree-one vortex solution.
status_evidence.claim: A simpler proof of uniqueness of the radial (degree-one) vortex solution has been obtained via Hardy decomposition methods.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of vortexless Ginzburg-Landau type minimizers in two dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes uniqueness for vortexless GL minimizers in 2D with techniques simpler than Pacard-Rivière's monograph.
status_evidence.claim: Simplified uniqueness results have been established for related Ginzburg–Landau settings.
